author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Iranian strikes damaged several U.S. military aircraft at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan this week, according to a U.S. official who spoke to Reuters.

The official said one A-10 Thunderbolt II lost a wing, while roughly eight F-15 aircraft sustained light damage and returned to service. The account did not identify the exact timing of each impact or provide a full estimate of repair costs.

U.S. forces fired about 30 Patriot interceptors to counter incoming missiles during the attack, the official said. The strike followed U.S. attacks on five Iranian crude carriers, which Washington said answered two attempted ballistic-missile attacks on a Navy warship.

The new damage assessment shows that the Jordan strike reached equipment on the base even as defenses responded. It also adds to concerns about aircraft losses and the rate at which air-defense interceptors are being used during the widening conflict. The situation remains developing, and the figures may change as military assessments continue.
dek: A U.S. official told Reuters that an A-10 lost a wing and about eight F-15s sustained light damage during this week’s attack.
headline: Iranian strike damages U.S. aircraft at Jordan base, official says
